methodology: Five individually keyed first-pass assessments. External locators are nonpublic comparison leads, not primary-text-verified citations. Distinguish legal contrast from direct narrative parallel; no dependence claims. Avoid counting the 9:8 and 9:10 repetition as independent external source proof.

records.summary: Protection for a polytheist seeking refuge to hear the divine message, followed by escort to a place of safety.

leads.note: Refuge for an escaped slave and freedom to reside contrasts with the Qur'anic temporary asylum and safe-conduct of a polytheist; different protected populations and legal rationales.

questions: Check Arabic terms ajara and ma'man against dated Arabic safe-conduct traditions; determine whether any pre-Islamic text addresses a religious opponent requesting hearing and escorted return.

records.summary: Treaty commitments at the Sacred Mosque; reciprocal upright conduct while the counterpart remains upright.

leads.note: Israelites honor their oath to the Gibeonites even after deception, whereas 9:7 conditions continued treaty relations on counterpart fidelity; neither text identifies the other's legal setting.

questions: Study Qur'an 9:4,7 together and critically assess reports identifying the treaty partners; compare Hebrew oath language only after edition-level check.

records.summary: Warning that opponents' agreeable speech conceals hostility and disregard for kinship or covenant.
questions: Screen early Near Eastern treaty denunciations for distinctive paired kinship-and-pact formula; generic warnings against hypocrisy are not sufficient to publish a source association.

records.summary: Exchanging God's signs for a small price and obstructing the divine path.

leads.note: Isaiah invites recipients to receive sustenance without money, unlike the Qur'anic charge of exchanging signs for gain; the shared monetary imagery is too generic to imply textual dependence.

questions: Check more specific Hebrew Bible passages about profiting from sacred instruction, e.g. Micah 3:11, against their complete context before promoting any comparison.

records.summary: Opponents are said to disregard kinship and covenant toward believers, described as transgressors.
questions: Check the exact rhetorical repetition with 9:8 and historical treaty context; do not double-count a generic covenant-breaking motif as a separate verified external source.

pending: Check primary texts in named editions, source dating and stable links before public promotion
